label: A tool the assistant calls
when: The assistant needs to do or read something it cannot today.

steps.text: Read the brief, the plan and the part of the map the plan touches (creator_map with the plugins named). Read the README of every plugin the plan touches.

Write the tests first, from the brief, in test/<name>.test.mjs: what the plugin must do, what it must refuse, and that it changes nothing while it is switched off. Stand-ins only: no real device, network, account, model or app data.
index.js: Config with `enabled` (false by default) and every field the page changes marked .volatile(); `export const inject` lists every service used as ctx.<service>.
Register the tool with `when` so it is offered only in the modes the plan names; its answer is {text} through a safely() wrapper that turns an error into a plain sentence; give it a timeoutMs.
Every program, web call, clock and approval goes through a function the third apply() argument can replace, so the tests use stand-ins.
If the tool must refuse something whatever the model says, decide it in a tools/pre-execute listener before next() and again as a final ctx.tools.guard.
client.js: a Settings page with the on/off switch, following docs/UI-STYLE.md (the app's colour variables only); no hook after an early return.
Write README.md: what the user gets, the rules and which of them code enforces, what is not built, how it was tested and what was not. Plain words.
Run creator_check: the trial copy loads the plugin without errors, its tests pass, the fit check is clear (or the user decided), and the trial install works. Fix and run it again until all four pass.
Report in plain words: what was built, what the checks showed, what was not verified, and what waits for the user's yes.
